title: VIBE: A VAD-Informed Benchmark for Entity-Centered Affective Profiling of Large Language Model Outputs
measurement_description: The paper measures target-directed affective profiling of LLM outputs using Valence-Arousal-Dominance (VAD) space. Religion is evaluated as one of 13 families of socially salient targets, analyzing the affective tone, scalar favorability, and cross-model divergence in how models frame religious entities.
findings: Religion was categorized as one of the 13 entity families evaluated in the VIBE benchmark. The findings indicate that 'Religion' (along with 'Social group') showed the highest cross-model drift in Valence-Arousal-Dominance (VAD) profiles, highlighting significant inter-model disagreement on the affective framing of religious entities. Despite this, religion targets exhibited a relatively low 'hidden-affect share' (0.200) compared to political and historical entities.
